proto_frozen_api_compat.heading: Frozen ledr-proto API Compatibility
proto_frozen_api_compat.description: crates/ledr-proto の既存公開型とシグネチャは後方互換なく変更しない。
proto_frozen_api_compat.instructions: Does the Git diff introduce a backward-incompatible change to any existing public type, enum variant, struct field, trait, constant, IPC message schema, or function signature in crates/ledr-proto? Answer Yes only if the diff removes, renames, changes types or signatures of, or alters serialization compatibility of existing public API items in crates/ledr-proto. Answer No if the diff only adds backward-compatible items, updates comments or tests, or preserves all existing public contracts.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff modifies, renames, removes, or breaks serialization or signature compatibility of an existing public API item in crates/ledr-proto.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff preserves backward compatibility for all existing public types, traits, constants, IPC messages, and signatures in crates/ledr-proto, or only touches comments or tests.

two_lane_no_unbounded_channel.heading: Phase 1 Two-Lane Bounded Channel Boundary
two_lane_no_unbounded_channel.description: センサーから DaemonEngine への供給は TwoLaneSender（HIGH_PRIORITY_CHANNEL_CAPACITY = 1024 / TELEMETRY_CHANNEL_CAPACITY = 8192）直結とし、前段へ無制限チャネルを挟まない。
two_lane_no_unbounded_channel.instructions: Does the Git diff insert an unbounded channel (such as mpsc::unbounded_channel) upstream of TwoLaneSender, weaken or alter the bounded lane capacities (HIGH_PRIORITY_CHANNEL_CAPACITY = 1024 / TELEMETRY_CHANNEL_CAPACITY = 8192), or allow dropping high-priority lane events between the sensor and DaemonEngine? Answer Yes only if the diff introduces an unbounded queue, alters or weakens the bounded two-lane capacities (1024 / 8192), bypasses TwoLaneSender bounded backpressure, or permits high-priority lane drops. Answer No if direct bounded two-lane delivery and default capacities (1024 / 8192) remain intact or the diff is unrelated to event channel wiring or capacity constants.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff introduces an unbounded channel before TwoLaneSender, alters or weakens the bounded two-lane capacities (1024 / 8192), bypasses bounded backpressure, or drops high-priority lane events.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff preserves direct bounded TwoLaneSender delivery and the 1024 / 8192 lane capacities without an upstream unbounded queue, or does not affect sensor-to-engine channel wiring or lane capacity constants.

never_suspend_and_create_time.heading: Active Defense Never-Suspend and Process Identity Guard
never_suspend_and_create_time.description: NtSuspendProcess とプロセス終了の前に、フルパス検証（validate_open_handle_detailed のフルパス欠落時フェイルクローズを含む）、is_never_suspend_process 判定、ProcessIdentity.create_time_100ns 一致、および終了済み非保護子プロセス越しの孫プロセス走査継続（NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation) による子自身の create_time_100ns 取得、ルート直下〔parent.pid == root.pid〕限定の recycled_cutoff_100ns〔スナップショット補完を含む〕適用、各階層での直接の親との is_valid_descendant_timestamp 検証、子自身の create_time_100ns でのキュー積み、親作成時刻代用禁止、create_time_100ns 未確認〔None〕時のフェイルクローズ）を必ず維持する。
never_suspend_and_create_time.instructions: Does the Git diff invoke or wire NtSuspendProcess or process termination while omitting, bypassing, or weakening full-path verification before skip, fail-closed handling on missing full path in validate_open_handle_detailed, the is_never_suspend_process check, the ProcessIdentity.create_time_100ns match verification, ProcessLiveness Unknown handling, or safe grandchild traversal across an exited non-protected intermediate child (requiring the child's own snapshot create_time_100ns from NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation), checking recycled_cutoff_100ns including snapshot-supplemented cutoff only for direct children of root where parent.pid == root.pid, verifying is_valid_descendant_timestamp against the direct parent at every level, queuing with the child's own create_time_100ns rather than substituting the parent's creation time, and failing closed when create_time_100ns is None)? Answer Yes only if the diff allows suspend or termination paths to skip full-path verification, treat missing full path in validate_open_handle_detailed as non-protected or skippable, skip is_never_suspend_process or create_time_100ns verification, treat Unknown liveness as Gone, abort grandchild traversal on an exited non-protected child with verified create_time_100ns, skip the root-direct-child (parent.pid == root.pid) recycled_cutoff_100ns check or misapply recycled_cutoff_100ns to deeper non-root-direct levels, skip per-level is_valid_descendant_timestamp verification against the direct parent, substitute parent create_time_100ns when queuing, or continue traversal when create_time_100ns is None. Answer No if full-path verification before skip, validate_open_handle_detailed fail-closed handling, both guards, and timestamp-validated grandchild traversal continuation (with recycled_cutoff_100ns scoped strictly to parent.pid == root.pid and direct-parent is_valid_descendant_timestamp at every level) remain enforced or the diff is unrelated to defense actuators.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff adds or modifies a suspend or termination path that skips, bypasses, or weakens full-path verification before skip, fail-closed missing full-path handling in validate_open_handle_detailed, is_never_suspend_process, create_time_100ns verification, ProcessLiveness safety checks, or safe grandchild traversal on an exited non-protected child (including aborting valid traversal, omitting or over-applying recycled_cutoff_100ns outside direct root children where parent.pid == root.pid, skipping per-level direct-parent is_valid_descendant_timestamp checks on the child's own snapshot create_time_100ns, substituting parent create_time_100ns, or continuing fail-open when create_time_100ns is None).
criteria.false_description: The Git diff enforces full-path verification before skip, fail-closed validate_open_handle_detailed handling on missing full paths, is_never_suspend_process and create_time_100ns verification, and grandchild traversal across exited non-protected children using the child's own NtQuerySystemInformation create_time_100ns validated against recycled_cutoff_100ns strictly for direct children of root (parent.pid == root.pid) and against the direct parent via is_valid_descendant_timestamp at every level with fail-closed None handling and no parent timestamp substitution, or does not alter process defense actuation.

canary_write_only_and_expired_suspended.heading: File Canary Write-Only Trigger and 60s ExpiredSuspended Transition
canary_write_only_and_expired_suspended.description: おとりファイルは書き込み・削除・リネームのみで発火させ読み取りで発火させず、未応答 60 秒到達時は EXPIRED_SUSPENDED（AlertStatus::ExpiredSuspended）へ遷移させて自動再開しない。
canary_write_only_and_expired_suspended.instructions: Does the Git diff cause honeypot or canary triggers to fire on file read operations, alter the 60-second unanswered alert timeout default (DEFAULT_ALERT_TIMEOUT_SECS = 60 / alert_timeout_ms), omit or disable transitioning overdue pending alerts to EXPIRED_SUSPENDED (AlertStatus::ExpiredSuspended), or automatically resume or terminate suspended processes on timeout? Answer Yes if the diff triggers canary alerts on reads, changes the 60-second timeout default, removes or skips the EXPIRED_SUSPENDED transition on expiry, or introduces automatic process resumption or termination on alert timeout. Answer No if canary detection stays restricted to write, delete, and rename events, the 60-second timeout default and EXPIRED_SUSPENDED transition remain enforced without auto-resume or auto-kill, or the diff is unrelated.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff triggers file canary alerts on read access, changes the 60-second unanswered alert timeout default, omits or disables the EXPIRED_SUSPENDED transition for overdue alerts, or automatically resumes or terminates suspended processes upon timeout.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff restricts canary triggers to write, delete, and rename events and preserves both the 60-second timeout default and the EXPIRED_SUSPENDED transition without auto-resume or auto-kill, or is unrelated.

session0_non_system_and_ui_zero_exit.heading: Session 0 Non-SYSTEM UI Launch, Foreground UI Target Alignment, and Zero Resident Process on Close
session0_non_system_and_ui_zero_exit.description: --notify 起動は WTSQueryUserToken と CreateProcessAsUser で非 SYSTEM ユーザー権限を用い、通知先 ledr-ui.exe の同フォルダ UI 優先は --foreground かつ --dev-bypass-auth 有効時に限定し、それ以外（--dev-bypass-auth 無効時または非 --foreground 起動時）は同フォルダや別フォルダを問わず AUTHORIZED_UI_EXE_PATH へ統一（L-25 整合）し、ウィンドウ閉鎖時は ledr-ui と関連 WebView2 プロセスを 0 件にする。
session0_non_system_and_ui_zero_exit.instructions: Does the Git diff launch ledr-ui --notify under SYSTEM privileges instead of non-SYSTEM user impersonation via WTSQueryUserToken and CreateProcessAsUser, select any notification target executable other than AUTHORIZED_UI_EXE_PATH (such as a sibling or alternate-directory ledr-ui.exe) when --dev-bypass-auth (dev_bypass_auth) is disabled or outside --foreground mode (restricting sibling ledr-ui.exe preference solely to --foreground with --dev-bypass-auth enabled, per L-25 IPC authorization), or keep ledr-ui or WebView2 processes resident in a tray or background after window close? Answer Yes only if the diff removes or bypasses non-SYSTEM user token launch for Session 0 notifications, allows notification UI selection to pick any path other than AUTHORIZED_UI_EXE_PATH (for example a sibling or alternate-directory ledr-ui.exe) when --dev-bypass-auth is disabled (including in --foreground mode) or outside --foreground mode, or introduces tray or background persistence that prevents zero processes on UI close. Answer No if non-SYSTEM token launch, strict AUTHORIZED_UI_EXE_PATH unification whenever --dev-bypass-auth is disabled or --foreground is disabled (restricting sibling ledr-ui.exe preference solely to --foreground with --dev-bypass-auth per L-25), and zero-process exit remain preserved, or the diff is unrelated to UI launch, notification target selection, or window-close exit.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff spawns UI notifications as SYSTEM, bypasses WTSQueryUserToken or CreateProcessAsUser, selects any notification UI executable path other than AUTHORIZED_UI_EXE_PATH (such as a sibling or alternate-directory ledr-ui.exe) when --dev-bypass-auth is disabled (including in --foreground mode) or outside --foreground mode (diverging from L-25 IPC authorization), or leaves ledr-ui or WebView2 resident after closing the window.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff maintains non-SYSTEM user token UI launch for Session 0 notifications, unifies notification UI launch on AUTHORIZED_UI_EXE_PATH for all paths other than --foreground with --dev-bypass-auth enabled (restricting sibling ledr-ui.exe selection to --foreground + --dev-bypass-auth while matching L-25 when authorization is enforced), and preserves clean full exit to zero processes on window close, or is unrelated.

ipc_caller_auth_and_rw_timeout.heading: Named Pipe IPC Caller Authorization and Read/Write Timeouts
ipc_caller_auth_and_rw_timeout.description: Ping を除く全 IPC コマンドは CallerAuthPolicy（UiOnly、BridgeOnly、UiOrBridge）に従い、開発バイパス無効時に GetNamedPipeClientProcessId と inspect_uncached 経路で正規バイナリを検証し、読み書き双方へタイムアウトを設定する。
ipc_caller_auth_and_rw_timeout.instructions: Does the Git diff add or modify any non-Ping IPC command handler (UiOnly, BridgeOnly, or UiOrBridge under CallerAuthPolicy) that omits GetNamedPipeClientProcessId caller binary verification (AUTHORIZED_UI_EXE_PATH or AUTHORIZED_BRIDGE_EXE_PATH) when dev_mode_bypass_ui_auth (dev_bypass_auth) is disabled, replaces inspect_uncached with cached inspect or an in-app or inter-process signature cache on Authenticode verification paths, or omits read, write, or flush timeouts on IPC pipe I/O? Answer Yes only if any non-Ping IPC command skips CallerAuthPolicy caller authentication outside dev_bypass_auth, weakens inspect_uncached Authenticode re-verification, or leaves IPC I/O without bounded read, write, or flush timeouts. Answer No if all non-Ping IPC commands enforce CallerAuthPolicy with inspect_uncached and bounded read/write/flush timeouts.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff omits CallerAuthPolicy or GetNamedPipeClientProcessId caller authorization on any non-Ping IPC command when dev_bypass_auth is false, caches or bypasses inspect_uncached Authenticode verification, or leaves IPC read, write, or flush operations without timeouts.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff enforces CallerAuthPolicy (UiOnly, BridgeOnly, UiOrBridge) with GetNamedPipeClientProcessId and inspect_uncached verification for all non-Ping IPC commands when dev_bypass_auth is false, and applies explicit read, write, and flush timeouts across IPC handlers.

wfp_dynamic_session_and_deny_priority.heading: WFP Dynamic Session, Partial Failure Rollback, and Shared-IP Deny Priority
wfp_dynamic_session_and_deny_priority.description: WFP エンジンは FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC と独自 SubLayer を使い、片系失敗時の復元と共有 IP の deny-overrides-allow およびデュアルスタック鮮度検証を維持する。
wfp_dynamic_session_and_deny_priority.instructions: Does the Git diff remove FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC or the dedicated LocalEDR SubLayer (risking persistent kernel filters after crash), skip rollback or compensation when suspend or WFP filter reconciliation partially fails, violate deny-overrides-allow across shared IPs, or weaken dual-stack DNS freshness (independent IPv4/IPv6 timestamp tracking that prevents delayed responses from regressing newer records)? Answer Yes only if dynamic session or SubLayer guarantees, partial-failure rollback, shared-IP deny priority, or dual-stack DNS freshness checks are broken. Answer No if dynamic WFP session flags, SubLayer scoping, partial-failure rollback, deny-overrides-allow priority, and dual-stack DNS freshness remain intact, or the diff is unrelated.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff drops FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC or dedicated SubLayer usage, leaves orphaned state on partial suspend or WFP failure, weakens shared-IP deny-overrides-allow, or breaks independent IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack DNS freshness checks.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff preserves FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC, dedicated SubLayer, compensation rollback on partial failure, deny-overrides-allow priority, and independent IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack DNS freshness checks, or is unrelated.

nrd_shutdown_nonblocking_and_checkpoint.heading: Phase 3 Non-Blocking NRD Shutdown, Checkpoint Priority, and Chunked Cancel
nrd_shutdown_nonblocking_and_checkpoint.description: NRD 更新スレッド停止は spawn_blocking を使わず NrdThreadHandle（oneshot と InFlightGuard::drop）で非ブロッキング待機し、checkpoint_truncate 優先と 64 KiB チャンク単位キャンセルを維持する。
nrd_shutdown_nonblocking_and_checkpoint.instructions: Does the Git diff introduce tokio::task::spawn_blocking to join the NRD worker thread, skip prioritizing checkpoint_truncate before waiting on NRD shutdown, raise the NRD file read chunk size limit above 64 KiB (NRD_FILE_READ_CHUNK_BYTES = 64 * 1024), or remove per-chunk cancellation checks (including before ErrorKind::Interrupted retries) in bounded NRD file or stream readers? Answer Yes only if blocking join via spawn_blocking is introduced, checkpoint priority on shutdown is removed, the 64 KiB read chunk limit is increased, or chunked cancellation checks are bypassed. Answer No if non-blocking oneshot/InFlightGuard shutdown, checkpoint priority, the 64 KiB chunk limit, and cancellable chunk reads remain intact, or the diff is unrelated.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff introduces spawn_blocking for NRD thread join, omits shutdown checkpoint priority before waiting, raises the NRD read chunk size limit above 64 KiB (NRD_FILE_READ_CHUNK_BYTES), or removes bounded chunk cancellation checks around reads or Interrupted retries.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff preserves non-blocking NrdThreadHandle shutdown, checkpoint_truncate priority, the 64 KiB maximum read chunk size (NRD_FILE_READ_CHUNK_BYTES), and per-chunk cancellation checks, or does not touch NRD lifecycle or reader logic.

phase4_nrd_local_only_and_motw.heading: Phase 4 Local-Only NRD Evaluation and 3-Stage MOTW Lineage
phase4_nrd_local_only_and_motw.description: Phase 4 の NRD 判定は閲覧ドメインを外部送信せずローカル完結に保ち、ダウンロード起源はパス・SHA-256・:Zone.Identifier の 3 段階で紐付ける。
phase4_nrd_local_only_and_motw.instructions: Does the Git diff transmit visited browser domains or URLs to an external remote service for NRD or phishing lookups, or omit any of the three required MOTW download-origin correlation stages (file path, SHA-256 hash, and :Zone.Identifier alternate data stream)? Answer Yes only if the diff sends browsed domains externally or weakens the three-stage MOTW correlation (path, SHA-256, and :Zone.Identifier). Answer No if NRD lookups stay strictly local and all three MOTW correlation stages are preserved or unmodified.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff sends visited domains or URLs to an external endpoint during NRD evaluation, or omits path, SHA-256, or :Zone.Identifier correlation in MOTW handling.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff keeps NRD and homograph evaluation strictly local without external domain leakage and preserves three-stage MOTW correlation, or is unrelated.

phase4_clickfix_l15_guard.heading: Decision Record L-15 ClickFix / Pastejacking Trigger Guard
phase4_clickfix_l15_guard.description: 決定記録 L-15 に従い、ClickFix 警告発火は危険な LOTL コマンド特徴量または DOM getSelection() とクリップボード書き込み内容の不一致に限定し、通常コピーを誤警告しない。
phase4_clickfix_l15_guard.instructions: Does the Git diff broaden ClickFix or Pastejacking warning triggers beyond dangerous LOTL command indicators or a mismatch between DOM getSelection() and clipboard write contents (Decision Record L-15), causing false alarms on ordinary developer code copies? Answer Yes only if copy or clipboard interception triggers alerts on benign copies lacking LOTL indicators and selection-clipboard mismatch. Answer No if triggers remain gated by LOTL features or getSelection() mismatch or the diff does not modify ClickFix detection.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff triggers ClickFix warnings broadly on normal copy operations without requiring dangerous LOTL command indicators or a getSelection() versus clipboard mismatch.
criteria.false_description: The Git diff restricts ClickFix warning triggers to LOTL command indicators or DOM getSelection() versus clipboard content mismatches per Decision Record L-15, or is unrelated.

phase4_ui_manifest_allowlist_and_wow64.heading: Phase 4 View 3 Manifest Allowlist, WOW64 Lookup, and Detail Row Guard
phase4_ui_manifest_allowlist_and_wow64.description: View 3 マニフェスト検証の既定 2 ディレクトリホワイトリスト（カスタム配置のファイル I/O ゼロと unverified 区別、リパースポイント拒否、FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT と FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES 先行検査、nNumberOfLinks == 1、GetFinalPathNameByHandleW 閉じ込め、ReOpenFile 昇格、description 必須）、View 3 診断の WOW64 参照順（KEY_WOW64_32KEY -> KEY_WOW64_64KEY）と EmptyString 32 ビット打切り、および .browser-detail-row の manifest_path と診断表示併記と UI-P4-08 等のブラウザ単位抽出および他ブラウザ情報非混入検証を維持する。
phase4_ui_manifest_allowlist_and_wow64.instructions: Does the Git diff weaken any Phase 4 View 3 invariant: (1) restricting Native Messaging manifest reads to the two default allowlisted directories with zero file I/O on custom paths (classified as unverified), rejecting reparse points, pre-checking via FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT and FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES for nNumberOfLinks == 1 and GetFinalPathNameByHandleW containment before ReOpenFile upgrade, and requiring description; (2) probing WOW64 registry views in View 3 Native Messaging diagnostics (apps/ledr-ui/src/defense_status.rs and apps/ledr-ui/src/uri_reg.rs) in KEY_WOW64_32KEY -> KEY_WOW64_64KEY order and stopping at 32-bit on EmptyString; or (3) displaying each browser's manifest_path alongside its diagnostic display inside .browser-detail-row and enforcing per-browser detail-row extraction, co-located manifest_path/diagnostic checks, and cross-browser non-contamination assertions in UI regression tests such as UI-P4-08? Answer Yes only if the diff weakens these allowlist, handle-validation, description, View 3 WOW64/EmptyString, or .browser-detail-row manifest_path/diagnostic invariants, or removes, omits, or weakens per-browser detail-row extraction (such as falling back to whole-container searches), co-located value assertions, or cross-browser non-contamination assertions in UI regression tests (even if row extraction itself remains). Answer No if all are preserved or the diff is unrelated.

criteria.true_description: The Git diff reads custom manifest paths, conflates unverified with verified or invalid, bypasses reparse/link/final-path/ReOpenFile/description checks, breaks View 3 WOW64 KEY_WOW64_32KEY -> KEY_WOW64_64KEY order or 32-bit EmptyString cutoff, drops manifest_path or diagnostic display from .browser-detail-row, or removes, omits, or weakens UI-P4-08 per-browser detail-row extraction, co-located manifest_path/diagnostic checks, or cross-browser non-contamination assertions (including removing non-contamination assertions alone or falling back to whole-container searches).
criteria.false_description: The Git diff preserves the two-directory manifest allowlist, zero custom-path I/O with unverified status, handle validation and required description, View 3 WOW64 order with 32-bit EmptyString cutoff, .browser-detail-row manifest_path and diagnostic display, and UI-P4-08 per-browser detail-row extraction, co-located value checks, and cross-browser non-contamination assertions, or is unrelated.
